plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-09-30 from the official UC Davis Department of Computer Science 'Sample Schedule: Computer Science - Starting in ECS 36A' (College of Engineering), https://cs.ucdavis.edu/sites/g/files/dgvnsk8441/files/media/documents/CS%20Sample%20Schedule%20-%20Starting%20in%20ECS%2036A.pdf. True program name is the BS in Computer Science (distinct from the department's separate 'Computer Science & Engineering' (CSE) major), College of Engineering. Program requirements cross-checked against the official UC Davis General Catalog page 'Computer Science, Bachelor of Science' (catalog.ucdavis.edu; states minimum 103 units for the CS major, 'minimum number of units required for the Computer Science Bachelor of Science is 103'). Course titles, units, and prerequisite chains cross-checked against the official CS Major Checklist (cs.ucdavis.edu) and the catalog's ECS course descriptions. UC Davis runs on the QUARTER system: the department's schedule totals 180 quarter units (12 quarters), which is set as total_credits. Transcription method: direct transcription of the department's published quarter-by-quarter grid into term rows; student-choice rows (linear algebra, lab science, probability, theory, upper-division composition, GE, CS electives, non-major electives) are modeled as choice:true placeholder slots with unique codes (LD-COMP, LA-REQ, SCI-1..3, PROB-REQ, THEORY-REQ, UWP-1, GE-1..8, ELECA-1..7, NME-1..10) and an options list drawn from the catalog/checklist. The schedule assumes the MAT 22A + MAT 22AL linear-algebra option (3+1 units); MAT 27A/MAT 67 are 4-unit alternatives with no lab. Caveats: this is the department's published sample (it notes it is 'only a guide' and impacted-course waitlists can shift quarters); the alternate-start 'ECS 32A' variant and the printed 'Alternate Option: ECS 50' (Sophomore) / 'Alternate Option: ECS 120' (Sophomore Spring) substitutions are not modeled as extra slots; GE placement follows the schedule's own GE cells, not the full College of Engineering GE breakdown.
